citations.quote: Received: 29 November 2024 / Revised: 17 April 2025 / Accepted: 18 April 2025 / Published online: 21 May 2025 © The Author(s) 2025

The study conducted a systematic review with a bibliometric analysis to examine the extent of utilization and effectiveness of model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and concurrent engineering (CE) in managing and optimizing system design factors in complex systems across various domains, including space, healthcare, as well as active and assisted living and smart environments.

To summarize, this systematic review examines the SE and CE approaches and methodologies within complex and challenging fields, assessing the role of MBSE in expanding model-based practices beyond the space sector, namely, also the healthcare and smart environments.
The objective of this systematic review (SR) study is to perform a comprehensive literature review and bibliometric analysis investigating whether MBSE and CE methodologies
maximize efficiency during the early lifecycle stages of complex SoI's, optimizing system design factors minimizing risks and optimizing performance in the later stages of the project.
The application of the PICO conceptual framework resulted in the question: "Are MBSE and CE methodologies efficient during the early stages of the lifecycle of complex
SoI's, optimizing system design factors and helping to minimize risks when compared to traditional engineering and/or design practices?".
Table 1 PICO framework for establishing a specific SR question and keywords identification

citations.quote: The steps of using the Rayyan platform were: importing libraries using RIS file extensions to transfer metadata about scientific publications between multiple platforms and software applications; extraction of RIS files from databases, or construction using the Zotero application (Takats et al. 2024), an open-source reference management software designed to help researchers collect, organize, cite, and share research materials; evaluation of each article by at least two evaluators; resolution of conflicts in special consensus sessions between evaluators; use of a waiting time of 2 weeks for requested access of publicly unavailable items.
Inclusion of in extenso publications only in English (11 articles were excluded).
Exclusion of duplicate articles from searches in different databases (237 articles were excluded).
Exclusion of articles in which the titles and/or abstracts are not relevant to the previously formulated question (443 articles were excluded).
Exclusion of articles that could not be accessed in full (for 29 articles requests for full text were sent, only 2 articles were provided by the authors).
Inclusion of external sources known by the authors independent of the database searches (8 articles were included).

Databases (n = 899): Scopus (n = 485), Web of Science (n = 227), IEEE (n = 160), PubMed (n = 27); Organisations (n = 8); Duplicate records removed (n = 229); Records screened (n = 670); Reports not retrieved (n = 27); Reports assessed for eligibility (n = 643); Studies included in review (n = 81); Reports of included studies (n = 81)

citations.quote: A structured quality appraisal process was applied to the selected studies to ensure methodological rigor and consistency. For this purpose, a standardized scoring framework designed for non-empirical data evaluation was used, namely the "Quality Scoring for Non-Empirical Studies" rubric developed by Laws and Winnard (2019). The framework assigns a score ranging from 1 to 11 and consists of two parts, a hierarchical classification of evidence types (maximum 7 points) and a series of criteria assessing the rigor and clarity of the article (maximum 4 points).
The scoring was performed independently by two reviewers, with the final quality score calculated as a mean of their total scores.
Data extraction was carried out by two reviewers.
For situations where there were conflicting items, a special session was organized in which the reviewers participated together with a team leader for the parties to reach a
consensus.

Data extraction can be seen in the Appendix section, Table 7, and the columns of the table refer to the following criteria: A. concurrent methodology; B. technological solution—the way in which the methodology was technically implemented; C. the purpose of using the methodology—based on the need to use the specified technology and the degree of complexity of the model used; D. population—technological maturity levels represented as TRL (technology readiness level); E. application type and general characteristics; F. the benefits of using the concurrent methodology; G. quality scoring—score obtained by completing the questionnaire "Quality scoring nonempirical data".

To perform the bibliometric analysis, the software VOSviewer version 1.6.20 (Van Eck and Waltman 2010) was used on Windows 11 Pro Operating System (OS). Additionally, to extract and add metadata to the articles collection and to export it as RIS file, the software Zotero version 6.0.36 was used on the same OS.

Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) was the prominently used concurrent methodology across many of the studies, implemented to streamline the development of complex systems. MBSE involves the use of comprehensive models to support system requirements, design, analysis, verification, and validation activities throughout the system's lifecycle. MBSE was identified as a primary methodology in approximatively 88% of the articles.

The technical implementation of methodologies like MBSE involves using specialized software tools to create, analyze, and manage complex system models. These tools support the creation of detailed diagrams and models that represent various system components and their interactions.

In the implementation process, systems engineers define the requirements, structure, behavior, and validation criteria of the system within these tools using the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) in 50% of the articles.

OPM, on the other hand, provides a more holistic approach by creating combined object-process diagrams that illustrate both the structure and behavior of systems in a single unified model. OPM was only used in five articles (6%) (Sharon and Dori 2012; Ramos et al. 2013; Mordecai and Dori 2017; Menshenin and Crawley 2019; Kohen and Dori 2021).

In aerospace, found in 16% of articles (Bandecchi et al. 2000; McVittie et al. 2012; Bhasin et al. 2013; Haveman and Bonnema 2013; Sindiy et al. 2013; Hennig et al. 2015; Fischer et al. 2018; Menshenin and Crawley 2019; Cohen et al. 2022; Fuchs et al. 2022; Huang et al. 2022; Brusa et al. 2023; Bussemaker et al. 2020), SysML allowed for the detailed modeling of spacecraft systems
The populations addressed in the reviewed studies encompass various sectors and technology readiness levels (TRLs).
The applications of MBSE methodologies span various domains, showcasing their broad applicability.

The relatively low percentage of studies in the advanced stages suggests that while MBSE is effective in the early and middle stages, its application in later stages, particularly in fully operational systems, may still be developing or is less frequently documented.

In the 81 articles analyzed in this study, there were a total of seven methodological benefits identified that were common among many of the findings (see Table 3). Efficiency gains were identified in 37 articles (45.7%) ,representing articles that directly claimed improved total project efficiency, fewer design iterations needed to arrive at the final solution, and/or increased resource utilization efficiency. Increased collaboration potential was identified in 30 of the articles (37.0%)
Co-occurrence analysis was performed to create keyword maps based on bibliographic data with full counting method setting.
According to the scoring rubric (see Table 6), 17.3% of articles (14/81) were assessed to be of poor quality (score of 6.5 or below).
Notably, CE and MBSE appear in two different clusters, indicating that despite their relationship, they occupy distinct conceptual and functional spaces in the literature.

Limitations are related to the fact that the selected research evidences were not experimentally tested and had a lack of quantitative data or instruments designed to assess the actual inclusion impact in the systematic review.

Another limitation is the fact that 27 items (4.25% of the articles) could not be retrieved. The authors considered two articles (1 conference paper and 1 journal paper) as duplicates during the screening stage, determining the text to be very similar and including only the single journal paper Menshenin and Crawley (2019).

A characteristic that made it difficult to develop the study is the relatively wide range of articles found due to the database search being performed without time restrictions and in a broad array of fields.

The findings of the study indicate that MBSE approaches consistently improve project outcomes by increasing efficiency, facilitating effective collaboration between different engineering disciplines, and reducing risks due to error, project time frame, and traceability issues.
The result of the study includes a comprehensive system model for the satellite power subsystem, verified and enhanced through real-time simulation.
System: Various applications including nanosatellites, sub-orbital planes, and hybrid motorcycles.
